wholeProduct.summary: TradeScout county discovery, claims-first accounts, gated requests/contact, business profiles and remaining isolated recovery work.

deliverables.outcome: Recover the county request and account authority loop on current production-source baseline.
deliverables.entry: Sign in or claim an account, then start a county-scoped service request.
deliverables.ending: Reopen the request and allow contact only following the persisted decision and permission.

proof.procedure: Run scripts/tests/recovery-transactions.native.ts against a fresh loopback test database.
proof.expected: Professional, booking and address operations preserve ownership, lineage, atomicity and locks.
proof.observed: Native transaction cases passed on the current integration before the final OAuth merge; complete combined release and browser validation remains pending.

journeySteps: Resolve authenticated provider-subject or claims-first account identity.
Create and reopen a county request with a persisted decision.
Preserve contact permission, address evidence and denial behavior.
constraints: Use existing TradeScout repository and canonical permission/storage/component owners; preserve County Map WIP and separate JW product changes.

completionClaims.claim: The recovered county request and account-authority loop is closed only after exact-candidate tests, native/browser evidence and deployment verification.

excludedFromActive: LSS saved-content release is the next dependent deliverable; JW presentation, County Map and other product stacks retain separate ownership.

deliverables.outcome: Release the reviewed LSS service profile and authorized native saved-content update against the delivered platform baseline.
Preserve remaining JW, County Map, membership, dependency and external-provider work for its own evidence-backed completion.

executionTarget.rationale: Existing TradeScout React/Express/Postgres contracts and Render production path own the workflow.
constraintsConsidered: Persistent requests and identity, explicit access decisions, append-only migrations and existing production repository.
